power-farming-displaces-tenants-childress-county-texas

An empty farmhouse stands in a wide field of plowed furrows in Texas in 1938, a farm where tractors had taken the place of families who once worked the land as tenant farmers. Dorothea Lange photographed it for the government to show how the Depression and new machines pushed families off the land.
ex-slave-with-a-long-memory-alabama

An elderly woman in Alabama who was born into slavery stands in front of her house in 1938. Dorothea Lange's photograph, taken during the Great Depression, honors a person who remembered a very different time in American history.
allie-mae-burroughs-hale-county-alabama

Allie Mae Burroughs, the wife of a cotton sharecropper, looks straight at the camera in 1936. Walker Evans took this photograph for a project that became the book Let Us Now Praise Famous Men, about poor farming families during the Depression.
frank-tengle-bud-fields-and-floyd-burroughs-cotton-shar

Three cotton sharecroppers sit together on a porch in Alabama in 1936. Walker Evans photographed families in Hale County for the government and a magazine, and the dignity in the faces made the photographs famous.
floyd-burroughs-cotton-sharecropper-hale-county-alabama
Floyd Burroughs, a cotton sharecropper in Alabama, looks into the camera in 1936. Walker Evans photographed him and his family for a famous project about rural poverty in the Great Depression.
jim-norris-homesteader-pie-town-new-mexico
Jim Norris, a homesteader in Pie Town, New Mexico, in 1940, photographed in rare color film by Russell Lee for the government. The color makes it feel as if the Depression is happening now.
school-children-singing-pie-town-new-mexico
Children sing together in a school in Pie Town, New Mexico, in 1940, in a color photograph by Russell Lee. Pie Town was a farming community in the Depression years.
american-gothic-washington-d-c

Ella Watson, a cleaning woman at a government office, stands with a mop and broom in front of an American flag in 1942. Gordon Parks, then a young photographer on his first assignment for the government, named it American Gothic as a tribute to Grant Wood's painting.
work-pays-america

A poster from the Works Progress Administration, the New Deal program that put millions of Americans back to work building roads, bridges and schools, as well as paying artists and writers. The workers and a wheat stalk show the idea that work lifts up the whole country.
ella-watson-at-home-washington-d-c
Ella Watson with her family at home in Washington, D.C., in 1942, in a photograph by Gordon Parks. He followed her through her day to show the life of a working mother in the Depression years.
the-beach-area-holland

Trucks and landing craft sit on a muddy beach in the Netherlands in 1945, painted by the Canadian war artist Alex Colville. Canadian troops helped liberate the Netherlands in the last year of the war.
the-nijmegen-bridge-holland

The great steel bridge at Nijmegen, which the Allies captured in September 1944 in the failed Operation Market Garden, arches across the river. Alex Colville, a Canadian war artist, painted it in 1944.
convoy-in-yorkshire-no-2
Army trucks roll along a road in the green hills of Yorkshire, England, where Canadian soldiers trained in 1944 before D-Day. Alex Colville was an official Canadian war artist.
landing-craft-assault-off-southern-france
Landing craft head toward the coast in the Allied invasion of southern France in August 1944, in a painting by the Canadian war artist Alex Colville.
canadian-armour-passing-through-ortona
A Canadian tank rolls through the shattered streets of Ortona, Italy, where Canadian troops fought a fierce street battle in December 1943. Charles Comfort was an official Canadian war artist.
night-air-attack-before-the-hitler-line

Flares and searchlights light up the sky over the Italian hills before an attack on the Hitler Line in 1944. Lawren P. Harris, an official Canadian war artist whose father was the famous Group of Seven painter Lawren Harris, painted it.
tank-convoy
A line of Canadian tanks rolls over a green landscape in 1944. Bruno Bobak served as a Canadian war artist and made sketches and paintings of what he saw.
canadian-women-s-army-corps-brass-band
Women of the Canadian Women's Army Corps play in a brass band in 1945. Molly Bobak was a Canadian war artist who painted women's role in the armed forces.
london-blackout
A dark London street during the wartime blackout, when all lights were turned off so that bombers could not find the city. Molly Bobak, a Canadian war artist, painted it in 1944.
an-lvt-comes-ashore-saipan
An LVT, a tracked amphibious vehicle, drives up a beach on Saipan in June 1944 during the fighting in the Pacific. William F. Draper was a US Navy combat artist who went into battle with the troops.
utah-beach
Landing boats, soldiers and equipment fill Utah Beach in Normandy after the D-Day landings of June 6, 1944. Joseph Gary Sheahan, a combat artist, painted the scene in watercolor.
formal-japan-surrender-aboard-the-u-s-s-missouri
On September 2, 1945, aboard the battleship USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, Japanese officials signed the surrender that ended World War II. Sidney Simon, a US Army artist, painted it.
loading-of-the-vultee-vengeance-planes
Ground crews load Vultee Vengeance dive-bombers in a busy scene from the war. Julien Binford painted it in 1944 as one of the US Army's combat artists.
assault-groups-taking-cover
American soldiers crouch among tropical trees during an assault in the Pacific in 1943. Aaron Bohrod was an official US Army war artist who painted the war in the Pacific.
gun-crew-loading-a-5-inch-38-caliber-gun

A sailor strains to load a big gun aboard a navy ship in 1940 in a powerful, poster-like painting. McClelland Barclay, an American illustrator who joined the US Navy as an artist, painted the sailors at work.
belsen-concentration-camp

A quiet field with open pits near the huts of Bergen-Belsen shows the horror of the Nazi concentration camp, which British and Canadian troops reached in April 1945. Alex Colville, a Canadian war artist, painted what he saw there, and the painting is a record of the Holocaust.
inferno
Fire sweeps through a battlefield in the Pacific in 1944 in a painting by William F. Draper, a US Navy combat artist, who painted battles he had seen.
a-man-on-the-moon-buzz-aldrin-apollo-11
Buzz Aldrin stands on the Moon on July 20, 1969, in a photograph taken by Neil Armstrong, whose reflection you can see in Aldrin's gold visor. It is one of the most famous photographs ever taken.
earthrise

Our blue Earth rises over the gray edge of the Moon in this photograph taken by astronaut William Anders on Christmas Eve 1968 during Apollo 8, the first time people had seen the whole Earth from another world. It changed how many people thought about the planet.
the-blue-marble
The whole Earth, round and blue and shining, photographed by the Apollo 17 astronauts on their way to the Moon in December 1972. The Blue Marble is one of the most reproduced images in history.
apollo-11-launch
A Saturn V rocket rises on a pillar of fire and smoke at the Kennedy Space Center on July 16, 1969, carrying the Apollo 11 crew to the Moon.
alan-shepard-in-the-freedom-7-capsule
Astronaut Alan Shepard sits in the tiny Freedom 7 capsule before his flight on May 5, 1961, when he became the first American in space. The flight lasted only 15 minutes.
buzz-aldrin-s-bootprint-on-the-moon
A single bootprint in the gray Moon dust, taken by the Apollo 11 astronauts to study the lunar soil. This close-up has become a symbol of the first human steps on the Moon in July 1969.
aldrin-looks-back-at-tranquility-base
Buzz Aldrin looks back at the landing site, Tranquility Base, in the bright gray landscape of the Moon, with the lunar module Eagle behind him. Neil Armstrong took the photograph in July 1969.
buzz-aldrin-descends-the-lunar-module-ladder
Buzz Aldrin climbs down the ladder of the Apollo 11 lunar module Eagle onto the Moon in July 1969. Neil Armstrong took the picture, and Aldrin was the second person to walk on the Moon.
buzz-aldrin-and-the-u-s-flag-on-the-moon
Buzz Aldrin stands beside the American flag on the Moon on July 20, 1969. The flag was held out by a wire so that it would look like it was flying in the airless Moon.
the-apollo-11-crew-armstrong-collins-and-aldrin
The crew of Apollo 11: Neil Armstrong, Michael Collins and Buzz Aldrin, in their white space suits. Armstrong and Aldrin walked on the Moon in July 1969 while Collins stayed in orbit.
astronaut-james-irwin-salutes-the-flag-apollo-15

Astronaut James Irwin salutes the flag beside the lunar module and the moon buggy, the lunar rover, in 1971. Apollo 15 was the first mission to use a rover on the Moon, and David Scott took the picture.
apollo-11-rolls-out-to-the-launch-pad
The huge Saturn V rocket for Apollo 11 is carried slowly toward the launch pad on a giant crawler in May 1969. At 110 meters tall, it was the most powerful rocket ever built at the time.
big-guns
Soldiers work on a big artillery gun in Vietnam in 1968 in a painting by David Fairrington. Fairrington was a member of the US Army combat art team, which sent artists to Vietnam to record the war.
radio-operator
A soldier carries a radio, the lifeline of a patrol, in a tall, bold painting by David Fairrington. He painted it in Vietnam in 1968 as part of the US Army's combat art program.
in-the-field
A soldier strides through golden grass in Vietnam in a painting of 1968 by David Fairrington. The Army's combat artists tried to show both the work and the feelings of the soldiers.
the-ladies
Vietnamese women in cone-shaped hats gather in a colorful, patterned scene by David Fairrington in 1968. The Army's combat artists also painted the Vietnamese people they met.
young-girls
Two Vietnamese girls lean close to each other in a gentle painting by David Fairrington from 1968. It shows the everyday life of civilians alongside the war.
cobra
A Cobra attack helicopter, one of the most important aircraft of the Vietnam War, is painted in dark glassy shapes by Stephen H. Randall in 1968 as part of the US Army combat art program.
mountain-climber
A helicopter waits on the ground in a muddy field in Vietnam, in a watercolor by Stephen H. Randall in 1968. Helicopters were everywhere in the Vietnam War, carrying troops and supplies.
over-there
Two soldiers lean over the edge of a bunker in Vietnam in a sketchy watercolor by Stephen H. Randall in 1968, made as part of the US Army's combat art program.
i-see-it
Medics treat a wounded soldier in a busy scene by Stephen H. Randall from 1968, one of the US Army combat artists sent to record the war in Vietnam.
